cells.name: OpenAI Responses API
cells.detail: responses.create / responses.parse / responses.stream, sync and async, streaming and non-streaming, function tools; max_output_tokens injected or clamped; usage settled from the terminal stream event
cells.notes: Added in kazenai 1.2.0. Live-verified 2026-10-13 against the paid OpenAI API through monitor(): responses.parse (text_format), responses.create and create(stream=True), and the responses.stream() helper, sync and async, on gpt-6-luna (openai 2.54.0 and 1.109.1) and parse/stream on gpt-6.1-sol (openai 2.54.0): real response, recorded cost equal to the pricing table on the provider-reported input/output tokens, and pre-dispatch BudgetExceeded. Opt-in test; not run in default CI. Refused before dispatch with UnsupportedModeError: background=True, previous_response_id / conversation / stored prompt (server-side input cannot be priced first), built-in tools (billed outside token usage), and resuming a stream by response_id. responses.compact and responses.connect stay blocked. LangChain/LangGraph Responses binding stays unsupported.

cells.name: OpenAI endpoints outside Control (Realtime, legacy Completions, Responses compact/connect, embeddings, images, audio, batches, fine-tuning)
cells.notes: Refused before dispatch with UnsupportedModeError on a monitored client since 1.2.0: client.realtime.connect, client.beta.realtime.connect, client.completions.create, responses.compact, responses.connect, and every other paid request sent through the monitored client without its budget check: a provider method, with_raw_response wrapper or client.request saved before monitor(), client.post(), a request triggered while another monitored client dispatches (authorization is per client), embeddings, images, audio, batches, fine-tuning, vector stores. The check runs at client.request() and again at the client's own view of its httpx client; a refusal at the second layer surfaces as APIConnectionError caused by UnsupportedModeError. Reads, deletes and free endpoints (files, uploads, moderations, token counting, cancel) still work. monitor(..., allow_unmetered=("/embeddings",)) sends named endpoints without a budget check; that spend is not counted. A client that was never passed to monitor() is not affected, even when it shares the same httpx client. Boundary: code that holds the provider key and builds another client, sends raw HTTP, or keeps the SDK's private _client from before monitor() is outside Control.

cells.name: LangGraph adapter / example
cells.notes: SqliteSaver/AsyncSqliteSaver local restart cells pass. Control requires prior explicit declare; the declaration is a caller assertion and does not intercept arbitrary raw clients in nodes. Default correlation side storage is local, temporary, and 24-hour bounded. Live-verified 2026-10-12 (langgraph 1.2.14) with gpt-6-luna/claude-sonnet-5-5/claude-haiku-4-5 and gpt-4o-mini/claude-sonnet-4-6/claude-haiku-4-5, including a 3-step workflow across 3 models and 2 providers. A graph declares every provider client its nodes use: declare_langgraph_control_boundary(graph, *clients) + wrap_graph(guarded_clients=[...]); each must be declared (decoys rejected). Live-verified with OpenAI + two Anthropic clients in one graph.

cells.name: CrewAI adapter
cells.notes: Certified in kazenai 1.2.0. Fixture cells (real CrewAI 1.15.26 objects over simulated providers): kickoff and akickoff on OpenAI and Anthropic with exact cost; denial before dispatch that CrewAI does not retry (raised as BudgetExceeded and HookAborted); OpenAI output_pydantic; LLM(stream=True); a two-provider crew on one SharedBudget; akickoff cancellation (no workflow.end, scope cleaned, an in-flight call settles exactly once); max_execution_time timeout; nested crews (child operation with parent_operation_id); concurrent kickoffs of two crews sharing one LLM; two adapters on one crew; kickoff_for_each; kickoff_async. Live-verified 2026-10-13 against the paid APIs (gpt-6-luna, claude-haiku-4-5): kickoff/akickoff on both providers, a two-provider crew on one SharedBudget, akickoff cancel, nested crews, and a two-provider crew on one Agent FinOps workflow budget (one reservation per LLM call, all settled, deny receipt): recorded cost equal to the pricing table on provider-reported tokens, and denial before dispatch. Refused under Control (UnsupportedFrameworkPath): any unbound agent/manager/planning/function-calling LLM, hierarchical crews without a bound manager, memory, knowledge and embedders, Crew(stream=True), llm_overlay, and non-native CrewAI LLM classes (Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, LiteLLM-routed). Not supported: Anthropic structured output (uses client.beta.messages, refused before dispatch), Responses auto_chain / built-in tools. Cancelling native akickoff stops the crew and emits workflow.error (terminal: cancelled), never workflow.end; CrewAI 1.15 runs agent LLM calls on worker threads, so a call already sent completes and is charged. kickoff_async runs kickoff on a worker thread: cancelling the awaiter does not stop it, so the crew finishes, its spend is checked and settled, and it emits workflow.end.
cells.detail: wrap_crew kickoff / native akickoff / kickoff_async; bind_crew_llm_client on native OpenAI and Anthropic LLMs (one budget for sync and async); every LLM the crew can call must be bound (guarded_clients=[...]); pin crewai 1.15.26

Gateway-owned streaming settlement is not live-verified.

cells.name: One budget across a multi-step, multi-model workflow
cells.detail: Steps on different models and providers share one Agent FinOps workflow budget via workflow_id; each step settles to its own model's price and is attributed by feature_id
cells.notes: Live-verified 2026-10-12: LangGraph plan(OpenAI) -> draft(Anthropic) -> review(Anthropic) repeated under one $0.02 workflow budget: 3 full passes, then the next step denied before dispatch (insufficient_capacity, deny receipt), settled total under the limit, per-step spend equal to each model's price. Two ways to share the cap: the FinOps authority (workflow_id + workflow limit; across processes and machines) or, in one process without FinOps, SharedBudget passed to every monitor() client (also live-verified 2026-10-12). Without either, each monitor() client has its own independent budget.

cells.name: SharedBudget across monitor() clients
cells.detail: monitor(..., budget=SharedBudget(max_usd=...)) makes several clients (sync, async, other providers, LangChain-bound) draw from one process-local cap; mutually exclusive with max_budget_usd
cells.notes: Live-verified 2026-10-12: a LangGraph workflow over gpt-6-luna/claude-sonnet-5-5/claude-haiku-4-5 and gpt-4o-mini/claude-sonnet-4-6/claude-haiku-4-5 drew from one wallet, completed 3 passes, then the next step was denied before dispatch; spend equalled the sum of each step's price. One process only; cross-process caps need Agent FinOps.

cells.name: Definitive provider rejection settles at $0

cells.notes: Live-verified 2026-10-12: a priced model unavailable on the account (claude-sonnet-4-5, HTTP 404) through monitor() and real Agent FinOps settled at 0 micros with no pending hold.

provenance_note: Maintained with kazenai-core. The readable view is docs/integrations/control-supported-matrix.md. Evidence entries name the dated verification run; test entries name the suite that guards the capability.
update_note: kazenai 1.2.0 / kazenai-finops 1.2.0 / kazen-event-schema 0.6.6 (on PyPI since 2026-10-28). Configuring Agent FinOps selects the Control lifecycle by default (reserve before dispatch, settle after, fail closed); the legacy check/reconcile path is opt-in, deprecated, and refused by hosted Agent FinOps. Control requires KAZENAI_TIER_MISMATCH_MULTIPLIER and provider clients with max_retries=0. OpenAI Responses API create/parse/stream, live-verified 2026-10-13 (gpt-6-luna, gpt-6.1-sol). CrewAI 1.15.26 certified (live-verified 2026-10-13). Security: every release from 1.0.1 to 1.1.3 lets some OpenAI calls on a monitored client skip the budget check (responses.parse, cached with_raw_response wrappers, legacy completions, Realtime, methods saved before monitor()); 1.2.0 guards or refuses them and refuses paid requests that skip the guarded methods (embeddings, images, batches...) unless allow_unmetered names them. Earlier evidence (kazenai 1.1.2, 2026-10-12): OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages (sync/async, streaming/non-streaming), LangChain, LangGraph, checkpoint resume, LiteLLM application- and gateway-owned accounting, multi-model workflow budgets, provider-rejection release and ordinary API keys are live-verified.
